promo-estate-licence.title: Estate agents: you are not licensed for that photo #shorts
promo-estate-licence.description:
From Canva's own Content License Agreement: "Releases are generally not obtained for Free Content, and some jurisdictions provide legal protection against a person's image, likeness or property being used for commercial purposes when they have not provided a release." Read the middle of that — image, likeness OR PROPERTY. Property marketing is commercial use, and the agreement puts the job of deciding whether a release is needed, and getting it, on you rather than on Canva. So: no stock people on the flyer, none on the window card, and never on a testimonial card, because a stock headshot beside "sold in two weeks, wonderful service" presents a model as a real client endorsing your business.

Not legal advice — agents are regulated differently in every market. This is the sentence to take to your broker.

promo-estate-hierarchy.title: Your window card gets three seconds #shorts
promo-estate-hierarchy.description:
Somebody walking past your window gives the card about three seconds, which buys you three pieces of information: the price, the location, and one photograph that makes them stop. The price goes in the largest type on the page — bigger than is comfortable, big enough to read from the pavement. Everything else — bedrooms, tenure, floor area, your number — belongs in a band across the bottom in type you would call too small. It is not too small. Nobody reads the details until the price and the picture have already done their job.

Full tutorial on the channel — the whole listing kit, and the licence clause most agents have never read.

promo-lock-compliance-band.title: Lock your licence number or it walks off the flyer #shorts
promo-lock-compliance-band.description:
Your name, your agency and whatever your market requires you to display go in the bottom band, set once. Then group those elements in Canva and lock the group. A locked group cannot be dragged out of place when you are working quickly on the fourth flyer of a busy week — which is the actual failure mode. Nobody deletes their licence number on purpose.

promo-three-exports.title: One flyer, three different exports #shorts
promo-three-exports.description:
The same design leaves three ways, and getting it wrong is the most common reason a flyer looks soft. Window cards and handouts: PDF Print, with crop marks and bleed if a shop is cutting it. Property portals: at the size they specify — every portal publishes a spec sheet. Social: build the set properly rather than re-exporting the flyer and hoping.
